Class LineGaugeElement

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<LineGaugeElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.LineGaugeElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class LineGaugeElement extends StyledElement<LineGaugeElement>
A DSL wrapper for the LineGauge widget.

A compact single-line progress indicator. 

lineGauge(0.75)
    .label("Progress: ")
    .filledColor(Color.GREEN)

CSS Child Selectors

The following child selectors can be used to style sub-components:

  • LineGaugeElement-filled - The filled portion of the gauge
  • LineGaugeElement-unfilled - The unfilled portion of the gauge

Example CSS: 

LineGaugeElement-filled { color: green; }
LineGaugeElement-unfilled { color: gray; }

Note: Programmatic styles set via filledStyle(Style) or unfilledStyle(Style) take precedence over CSS styles.

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size

      public Map<String,String> styleAttributes()
      Description copied from interface: Styleable
      Returns the style attributes for attribute selector matching.

      Attribute selectors like Panel[title="Test"] match elements based on their style attributes. This method returns a map of attribute names to their values.

      Common attributes include:

      • title - the element's title
      • label - the element's label
      • placeholder - the element's placeholder text
